items.claim: The test 'creates new stack if original error has no stack' now builds `original` with `new Error('original')`, which has a stack, so it no longer tests the no-stack case it names.
items.consequence: A probe confirmed `e.stack === original.stack` for this input, so the test takes the same `originalError.stack` branch as the test above it and its only stack assertion (`to.be.a('string')`) passes trivially. If the fallback in GraphQLError.js (lines 201-208) for a stackless original error regressed, e.g. left `stack` undefined, the suite would stay green. To satisfy Flow and keep coverage, delete or undefine the stack on the Error (`const original = new Error('original'); delete original.stack;`) and assert `e.stack !== original.stack`.

items.claim: Only the `declare class` constructor was widened to accept `null` for `nodes`; the implementing function at line 94 still declares `nodes?: $ReadOnlyArray<ASTNode> | ASTNode | void`.
items.consequence: The two signatures for the same constructor now disagree: the public type permits `new GraphQLError('msg', null)` while the implementation annotation says null is not allowed. Anyone reading or type-checking the function body (or generating typings from it) sees the stale narrower contract, and the next edit can easily update one signature without the other. Line 94 should be updated in the same change.

items.claim: The shared fixture (`parse(source)` plus two `invariant` calls) now runs at module top level instead of inside the tests.
items.consequence: If the parser regresses and `parse` throws, or an invariant fails, the exception is raised while mocha is loading the file. Because `npm run testonly` loads every test file before running, that aborts the whole run with a load error instead of reporting failures in the three or four affected tests, and the unrelated tests in this file (name/message/stack, path, extensions) never run. Moving the setup into a `before()` hook or a helper function keeps the failure localised.

items.claim: 'serializes to include message and locations' no longer parses a plain single-line string (`parse('{ field }')`); it reuses the shared multi-line `Source` fixture.
items.consequence: Every location test in the file now runs on the same `Source` object and the same node (line 2, column 3). The only case that built a GraphQLError from a document parsed from a raw string, and the only one asserting a line-1 location for a non-zero offset, is gone. A regression specific to string input or first-line column computation would no longer be caught here.

items.claim: Declaring the whole error as `const e: any` (also at line 41) turns off the Flow checking this PR is enabling for the `locatedError(e, [], [])` calls.
items.consequence: Because `e` is `any`, the `locatedError` call and the `deep.equal(e)` comparison are unchecked. If `locatedError`'s first parameter type changes, these two tests still type-check and the `@flow strict` header gives false confidence. A narrower form keeps `e` typed as Error: `Object.assign(new Error('...'), { path: [], ... })`, or cast only at the property writes (`(e: any).path = ...`).

items.claim: A bare `// $FlowFixMe` with no explanation suppresses the Flow error on the `String.raw` tagged template instead of removing the cause.
items.consequence: The suppression covers the whole next line, so any future type error in `inspect('"')` or in the expect chain on that line is hidden too, and nothing records why it is there. The expected value can be written without `String.raw` as the plain literal `'"\\""'` (or `JSON.stringify('"')`), which needs no suppression.

items.claim: The parse / take first definition / invariant / take first field sequence is copy-pasted for A and B, and the variables `opA`/`opB` hold object type definitions, not operations.
items.consequence: Maintenance cost: the two blocks at lines 52-64 and 66-78 differ only in the SDL text and source name and must be edited in lockstep. The `op` prefix (carried over from the operation-node pattern in GraphQLError-test) misleads readers into expecting an OperationDefinition where the invariant checks `Kind.OBJECT_TYPE_DEFINITION`. A small helper such as `getFieldType(sdl, name)` would remove the duplication, and `typeA`/`typeB` would be accurate names.

items.claim: The new `invariant(...)` calls omit the `message` argument that `jsutils/invariant` declares as required (`message: string`); the same applies at printError-test.js lines 63, 77 and 80.
items.consequence: If the fixture shape changes (for example `definitions[0]` is not an operation, or `fields` is empty), the invariant throws `new Error(undefined)`: an error with an empty message, raised at module load in this file, with nothing saying which precondition failed. Passing a short message (e.g. 'expected operation definition') makes the failure diagnosable.

items.claim: `$ReadOnlyArray<ASTNode> | ASTNode | void | null` on an already-optional parameter spells out a maybe type by hand, unlike the sibling parameters.
items.consequence: Readability and consistency cost: every other parameter in this constructor uses the `?T` maybe form (`source?: ?Source`, `positions?: ?$ReadOnlyArray<number>`). `nodes?: ?($ReadOnlyArray<ASTNode> | ASTNode)` or `nodes?: $ReadOnlyArray<ASTNode> | ASTNode | null` would mean the same thing; the hand-rolled union with a redundant `void` invites the kind of drift already visible against the implementation signature at line 94.
